outcome: Haemolytic Disease of the Foetus and Newborn (HDFN)
cohort: The study included 121 mothers and their children who were managed by the National Reference Centre in Perinatal Hemobiology for alloimmunization and maternal-foetal incompatibility for the Rhc antigen.
finding: During pregnancy, anti-c antibody concentration ≥7.5 IU/ml and titre ≥4, as well as high intensity of the quantitative direct antiglobulin test at birth, were associated with HDFN and severe HDFN.
